overview: The L293D does the same basic job as an L298N — two H-bridge channels for driving DC motors — but comes as a plain 16-pin DIP chip you can push straight into a breadboard, rather than a pre-assembled module with screw terminals. Its current rating is much lower (fine for small hobby motors, not for anything beefy), but it has one genuine advantage baked in: built-in flyback diodes on every output, protecting the chip from the voltage spikes a motor generates when it's switched off. It's also the chip underneath the classic Arduino Motor Shield.
simpleSummary: A chip that lets a microcontroller control two DC motors, in a plug-into-breadboard form.

specifications.flybackDiodes: Built in (no external protection diodes needed)

pinMap.name: 1,2EN
pinMap.function: Enable pin for channel 1 (motor A) — must be HIGH for outputs 1Y/2Y to respond to inputs.

pinMap.name: 1A
pinMap.function: Direction input for motor A, paired with 2A.

pinMap.name: 2A
pinMap.function: Direction input for motor A, paired with 1A.

pinMap.name: 3A
pinMap.function: Direction input for motor B, paired with 4A.

pinMap.name: 4A
pinMap.function: Direction input for motor B, paired with 3A.

pinMap.name: VCC1
pinMap.function: Logic supply voltage for the chip's internal control circuitry.
pinMap.gotcha: Easy to confuse with VCC2 — VCC1 is logic power, VCC2 is motor power, and they're often different voltages.

pinMap.name: VCC2
pinMap.function: Motor supply voltage, switched through to the outputs.

pinMap.name: GND
pinMap.function: Ground pins (multiple, also serve as the chip's heat-dissipation path).
pinMap.gotcha: The GND pins double as the thermal path out of the chip — leave adequate copper/ventilation around them in a permanent build.

useCases.title: Breadboard-prototyped small robot
useCases.scenario: Drive two small motors directly from a breadboard circuit without needing a separate driver module.

useCases.title: Arduino Motor Shield projects
useCases.scenario: The classic Arduino Motor Shield is built around this exact chip.

oftenConfusedWith: L298N (higher current, module form factor with screw terminals)
oftenUpgradedTo: L298N or BTS7960 for motors drawing more than ~600mA
